newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schering says not affected by patent recall.
newsitem.headline: Schering says not affected by patent recall.

text.p: German drugs group Schering AG said on Thursday it was not affected by the European Patent Office's decision to revoke a patent issued to another German group for the possible treatment of multiple sclerosis.
"We are not affected by this move," Schering spokeswoman Christiane Schulz told Reuters.
On Wednesday, US-based Biogen said the Opposition Division of the European Patent Office (EPO) had revoked a patent issued to Dr Rentschler Biotechnologie GmbH.
That patent related to a specific cell line, production method, and form of recombinant beta interferon for multiple sclerosis.
Schulz said that while Schering was involved in a cooperation with the group Dr. Rentschler Biotechnologie GmbH, Schering had never held a license for the revoked patent.

Schering's multiple sclerosis drug Betaferon was until recently the only product sold to treat the chronic progressive disease of the central nervous system. Biogen last year launched a rival product Avonex.

Biogen had filed the opposition with the European Patent Office. "Although the revoked Rentschler patent did not cover (Biogen's) Avonex (Interferon beta-1a), we filed an opposition in order to remove uncertainty from the marketplace," said Jim Tobin, Biogen's president and chief executive officer in a press release.
According to Biogen, the Office ruled that the Rentschler patent was not valid on the grounds that the patent claims lacked novelty and inventive step.

Biogen said that the EPO had revoked the patent for recombinant beta interferon licensed to Schering that covered a broader method of producing the compound. But Schering said it did not hold such a license.
Rentschler has the opportunity to appeal the Opposition Division's decision to the EPO's Technical Board of Appeal, Biogen said.
Schering's share price was down 1.55 marks at 163.35 as the broader market was also down 0.08 percent at 3,393.36 points
